Quirk Training and Technique.text: Professional heroes treat a Quirk as a skill. Training starts with control: switching the Quirk on and off cleanly, aiming it, holding it steady while moving and using it under stress without hurting allies. Then come output and endurance. Many heroes think of output as a dial rather than a switch and train to use exactly as much power as a situation needs; some measure it as a percentage of their maximum and drill holding fixed levels. Hero training also builds the body, since stronger muscles, lungs and bones raise what a Quirk can safely do. From that base heroes develop special moves: named, rehearsed techniques that apply a Quirk in one reliable way, such as a long-range shot, a burst of speed, a restraining hold or a wide-area rescue technique. The name helps a hero call up the move under pressure and lets teammates read it instantly. Special moves never add a power the Quirk lacks; they are practiced uses of what it already does. Support gear is the other half. Heroes work with designers to build costumes and equipment around their Quirks: nozzles that focus a spray, armor that carries recoil, tools that cover a weakness. Hero academies teach all of this as a curriculum, with specialist teachers, measured tests and regular drills, and pros keep training for their whole careers.
